title: What Is Inflation?
paragraphs: Have you noticed that many things cost more than a few years ago? When the prices of most goods and services rise over time, economists call it inflation.

Inflation means that the same amount of money buys less than before. To measure it, countries follow the prices of a basket of common things, such as food, rent, clothes and transport, and see how much the total changes in a year.

Prices can rise for different reasons. Sometimes people want to buy more than shops can offer. At other times, costs for companies go up, for example when energy becomes expensive, and they ask for higher prices.

Central banks try to keep inflation low and stable. Many aim for about two percent a year. When inflation is too high, they usually raise interest rates, so borrowing becomes more expensive and people and companies spend less.
